TDY.thesis_one_line: A disciplined serial acquirer of niche instrument, sensor and defense-imaging franchises, compounding earnings at low leverage, priced below what its usual growth-plus-M&A algorithm can deliver.
kill_criteria: Digital Imaging segment organic revenue growth falls below 5% YoY for two consecutive quarters.
Funded backlog book-to-bill ratio drops below 1.0x for two consecutive quarters (it has been >1.0x for 11 straight quarters as of Q2'26).
Net debt/EBITDA rises above 2.5x post-Varex-close without a disclosed deleveraging plan within 18 months.
The Varex acquisition is blocked by regulators, terminated, or produces adjusted-EPS dilution beyond what management guides at signing.
A goodwill impairment charge is recorded against any acquired business (goodwill is 57% of consolidated assets).
key_adverse_facts: Unclosed $1.1B Varex Imaging cash acquisition (announced 2026-08-10, expected close early 2027) carries real regulatory-approval, financing and integration risk not yet resolved.
ROE (8.9%) and b1 quality percentile (0.27) are depressed by a large accumulated goodwill base (57% of consolidated assets) from two decades of M&A.
Digital Imaging/defense revenue depends on U.S. government budget cycles (continuing resolutions, program timing).
data_conflicts: b1 composite percentile (0.31, decile 4) is middling even though the filed fundamentals (9.8% revenue growth, 160bp YoY margin expansion, two consecutive guidance raises) look stronger than a decile-4 quant rank would suggest; the gap traces mainly to a low ROE/quality percentile driven by legacy M&A goodwill rather than weak underlying economics.
TDY.confidence_in_thesis: medium - filed growth, margin trend and low leverage are solid, but the still-unclosed Varex deal is a specific, unresolved event risk that caps conviction at half weight

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 systematic valuation row exists for TDY in v1_valuation_table.csv/v1_valuation.json, so there is nothing to reconcile against; this dossier's own reverse-DCF (implied 10y FCF growth ~6.6% vs. an ~9% base case) is the only quantitative valuation view available and reads attractive.

TDY.scenario_basis: Entry EV/FCF 26.4x on TTM FCF $1,142.1M (EV $30,156.2M = mkt cap $28,469.3M + net debt $1,686.9M); TDY pays no dividend; bear -2%/base 9%/bull 16% 3y FCF CAGR with exit EV/FCF of 20x/26x/30x respectively.

TEL.thesis_one_line: A diversified connector and sensor maker is riding a real, order-book-confirmed AI-datacenter and electrification boom; on programme inputs the price already asks for about 7% a year of free-cash-flow growth, in line with the base case, so no valuation cushion.
kill_criteria: The DDTC export-control investigation results in a fine, penalty or remediation order exceeding $50M, or a formal enforcement action is announced.
AI/data-center order momentum reverses (orders decline sequentially for two consecutive quarters) rather than continuing to pull the $3B FY2027 target forward.
Automotive or Industrial segment organic revenue growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters.
Net debt/EBITDA rises above 2.0x (from an estimated ~0.9-1.0x today) without a clearly disclosed reason such as large debt-funded M&A.
A further one-time tax or legal charge exceeding $500M recurs within the next four quarters.
key_adverse_facts: TE Connectivity has made a voluntary self-disclosure to the U.S. State Department's DDTC regarding past export-control compliance and is cooperating with an ongoing investigation whose timing, outcome and potential fines cannot be predicted.

A one-time non-cash tax charge tied to the 2025 Ireland redomicile and OECD global-minimum-tax rules collapsed FQ2 FY2025 GAAP net income to $13M (EPS $0.04), a real filed data point, not an error, but evidence the tax-law sensitivity is structural.
Automotive and Industrial end-markets, still the majority of revenue, could offset the current AI/data-center tailwind in a normal cyclical downturn.
TEL.confidence_in_thesis: medium - order-book acceleration is strong and the DDTC matter is bounded, but DVH1 recompute shows implied growth in line with base (6.9-7.6% vs 7%), and the Astrodyne TDI $1.4bn deal adds debt

TMO.thesis_one_line: The largest life-science tools and services platform is genuinely re-accelerating on a bioprocessing and academic-funding recovery, but the price already implies more growth than a fair base case delivers.
kill_criteria: Organic revenue growth (ex-recent M&A) falls below 4% YoY for two consecutive quarters.
Adjusted EPS guidance is cut from the current $24.93-$25.33 FY2026 range.
Estimated net debt/EBITDA rises above 3.5x (from an estimated ~3.3-3.4x today) without a disclosed deleveraging plan.
Bioprocessing/pharma-services order momentum (book-to-bill) turns negative for two consecutive quarters.
The reverse-DCF implied-growth gap versus this dossier's 8% base case widens further without a fundamental acceleration to justify it.
key_adverse_facts: Consolidated total debt rose from $39,172M (2025-12-31) to $42,284M (2026-06-27), a ~$3.1B six-month increase this pass could not fully trace to a single disclosed transaction, alongside cash falling from $9,852M to $4,064M.
Buybacks accelerated sharply to a cumulative $4.0B through Q2 2026 (from ~$3.0B for all of FY2025), funded partly by the cash drawdown noted above.
b1 momentum percentile is weak (0.10) even after two consecutive guidance raises - an unresolved tension between the quant data and the narrative.
GAAP-to-adjusted EPS gap (~29% of GAAP EPS) was not independently decomposed line-by-line from the 10-Q's non-GAAP reconciliation in this pass.
data_conflicts: b1 momentum percentile (0.10, weak) sits in tension with two consecutive quarters of guidance raises off real beats; this dossier does not resolve the conflict and flags it for the next review.
TMO.confidence_in_thesis: medium - business quality and the near-term recovery are well evidenced, but the valuation gap and the unexplained debt increase are reasons to wait, not to add
